output.reason: Two days of black tarry stools with lightheadedness on standing in a 58-year-old suggests ongoing upper GI bleeding with possible significant blood loss, requiring immediate emergency assessment, labs and endoscopy capability.
output.patientMessage: Go to the emergency department now. Black, tarry stools usually mean bleeding in your upper gut, and feeling lightheaded when you stand can mean you've lost a significant amount of blood. Have someone drive you or call 911 — do not drive yourself. If you faint, vomit blood or material like coffee grounds, or feel your heart racing, call 911 immediately.
differential: Upper GI bleeding (e.g. peptic ulcer, gastritis, varices)
Small bowel or right colonic bleeding source
